title: Sector Nine Rising Revisited
premise: Marguerite Marchetti was decanted to inherit a dead woman's memories, her debts, and her unsolved murder—her own. Administering the failing colony of Sector Nine, he records the slow collapse of a place Earth officially deleted from its ledgers. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, he traces it to the reactor vault where the original Marguerite died, and uncovers proof of a massacre the corporation erased from every record. As the reactor's countdown accelerates toward a 'routine decommissioning' that will bury the evidence, Marguerite must choose between the duty of obedience he was cloned for and the love he feels for Ilsa, the signal's transmitter, a descendant of the erased. He broadcasts the truth in the extinct language, dooming his chance at rescue but freeing Sector Nine's survivors—and finally himself—to be remembered.
about_author: Paloma Nakamura is a former archival technician who spent six years cataloguing decommissioned off-world settlement records before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted weather station in the Azores, where she keeps a shortwave radio tuned to frequencies nobody uses anymore.

chapters.title: The Inheritance of Dead Air
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He begins his 400th day as Sector Nine's administrator, recording the colony's decay in a log only he will ever read. Flashbacks of the original Marguerite's memories bleed into his routine—her last day, her last argument, the vault door. He is dutiful, invisible, alone. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath bureaucratic calm.

chapters.title: Census of the Forgotten
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A supply ship skips Sector Nine again; Earth's manifests list the colony as closed. He inventories the 211 remaining settlers, most of them descendants of workers the corporation never registered. Ilsa Reyes, the hydroponics chief, challenges his silence about their status. Emotional beat: the first crack in his neutrality—he cares.

chapters.title: A Voice in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. During a reactor diagnostic, his instruments catch a repeating distress signal in Láadan-descended colony pidgin, extinct for two centuries. It originates inside the reactor vault—the sealed site of the original Marguerite's murder. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into violation; someone has been calling from a tomb.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: Alternating Marguerite and memory-fragments POV. The inherited memories sharpen: the original Marguerite had found mass graves beneath the reactor, evidence of the Founding Purge, and was killed for it. Marguerite realizes he wasn't cloned to continue her work—he was cloned to bury it. Emotional beat: identity shaken; he is a weapon wearing her face.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Grandmother's Silence
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa reveals her family has passed down the extinct language orally for generations, forbidden since the Purge. She has been transmitting the signal for years, hoping someone outside would listen. She and Marguerite grow close translating the archives she's hidden. Emotional beat: love kindling inside shared grief and shared secrecy.

chapters.title: The Countdown Begins
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Corporate command, alerted by his diagnostic queries, orders an accelerated 'decommissioning': the reactor will scuttle the vault—and the graves—in eleven days. His handler reminds him of his purpose with chilling tenderness. Emotional beat: the cage of duty closing; obedience was always the design.

chapters.title: Eleven Days of Evidence
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Ilsa's POV, alternating. They race to extract and verify the buried records: bone fragments, a child's shoe, the original's hidden data core. Corporate auditors arrive early, suspicious. Marguerite must lie to the people he was built to obey. Emotional beat: terror and resolve entwined; the case becomes personal twice over.

chapters.title: The Handler's Face
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Confronted by his handler, Marguerite learns he is the seventh clone—the previous six were decommissioned when they learned too much. The handler offers him erasure with dignity if he surrenders the evidence. Marguerite refuses, and the handler locks down the colony. Emotional beat: the original's murder finally understood—he is being murdered in slow motion, again.

chapters.title: Broadcast from the Vault
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Ilsa's POV, converging. With hours before the reactor's countdown completes, they breach the vault, recover the massacre proof, and Marguerite transmits everything in the extinct language on every open band—untranslatable to corporate filters, legible to the descendants scattered across the colonies. Emotional beat: triumphant defiance; a dead tongue becomes a living alarm.

chapters.title: Sector Nine Rising
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV, epilogue-like. The broadcast spreads; descendant communities across three systems rise to demand recognition, and an independent tribunal arrives as the reactor dies harmlessly, its decommissioning overridden. Marguerite, stripped of his administrator's duty, chooses to stay—not as an inheritance, but as himself. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into belonging; love and identity, finally, freely chosen.
